title: Jim Nantz shares memorable broadcasting moment from Pebble Beach over 40-year career - CBS Sports
description: With the PGA Tour calendar winding down, Nantz reflected on the year and a favorite memory
body:
With the PGA Tour calendar winding down, Nantz reflected on the year and a favorite memory

        The end of a season inevitably brings a sense of nostalgia. Like a school year ending -- when ironically most are beginning -- the culmination comes with thoughts of what has been. Superlatives are given out. Memories are shared. Plans for the future go from pencil to pen to gone in a blink of an eye.The PGA Tour is no different. Like any other organization or group, the calendar comes for them with the FedEx Cup Playoffs representing the final salvo for what was an eventful, even surprising, 2026 campaign. Superstars and household names won. Young guns fired on all cylinders. Major championships were claimed by both perennial contenders and outsiders who gained the inside track.Much of the story has unfolded on CBS airwaves just as the remaining two tournaments -- the BMW Championship and the Tour Championship -- of the FedEx Cup Playoffs will. At the helm for it all has been legendary broadcaster Jim Nantz amid a season that marked No. 40 since his first call at the Masters in 1986.Yes, that Masters.Having experienced a lifetime of calls and a lifetime of once in a lifetime moments from those swinging the clubs, Nantz would not divulge if there has been a favorite broadcast of his to be a part of."The next one," Nantz said. "I love them all."
Instead, he did what he did best and told a story. This one about the old Crosby Clambake as it was called back then, now known as the AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am. While the whimsical nature of the event has passed by and those in the pro-am portion of the tournament across the first 36 holes are more C-Suite than C-list, there was a time, and who better to explain how his original answer formed than Nantz himself."One time, I was a part of the CBS crew early in my career at Pebble [Beach]. I never forgot this line," Nantz said. "Phil Harris played this boozy, kind of always looked like a guy that was coming in and out of bars, and that's not cool today, I get that. "But actually, on the air, on our air one time, Jack Lemmon hit a shot at 18 at Pebble Beach, down off the rocks and into the ocean and [Pat] Summerall intone, 'That's Lemmon on the rocks,'. [Ken] Venturi said, 'Sounds like a drink I had last night in the taproom.' "And with that, he turned to Phil, who was now playing the role of Bing [Crosby]. Bing had just recently passed in the last 10 years. He says, 'You know, Phil, I've always wanted to ask you, you're a renowned drinker, what's your favorite drink?'
"And he said on CBS, 'The next one.'"

        Max Holloway only sees empty threats from Conor McGregor. In the aftermath of a disappointing conclusion to their fight at UFC 329, Holloway sees just a loudmouth where a brash, talented young fighter once stood.Holloway and McGregor headlined International Fight Week this year. Nearly 16 million people across the U.S. and Latin America tuned in for the monumental card. Unfortunately, the fight fizzled immediately once the spectacular entrances concluded. McGregor injured himself with the first kick he threw, and the fight was waved off a little more than a minute later. McGregor went on a crisis management tour in the weeks after. He advocated for a no-contest ruling, and claimed his "generational beating" of Holloway was only postponed to next year. Holloway can't help but laugh at McGregor."It's just crazy for the dude to be talking about how it was slippery because of the dry ice," Holloway said on his YouTube channel, referencing the substance for their elaborate entrances. "I don't know what he's talking about because I didn't fall. 
"Him talking about this 'generational beating.' Dude is delusional because, to me, he felt slow in there. He looked old. If there was gonna be a generational beating, it wasn't gonna be on his end."Holloway has three directions in mind for his next fight. "Blessed" would like a welterweight or lightweight title shot. He's also open to completing the McGregor trilogy, something he also advocated during his post-fight interview.
"If it's a title shot, in either weight class, sign ya boy up," he said. "If it's a Conor McGregor fight again, I'll sign the dotted line.   UFC, I'm owed the Conor McGregor belt, the money belt, so you guys gotta send me that."

title: Klay Thompson expected to sign with Heat after buyout from Mavericks, per report - CBS Sports
description: The veteran wing will provide the Heat with much-needed shooting around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo

The veteran wing will provide the Heat with much-needed shooting around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo

        The Dallas Mavericks announced on Friday that they had reached a buyout agreement with Klay Thompson, making the sharp-shooting wing a late addition to the free agent market. Shortly after the announcement, ESPN reported that Thompson is expected to sign with the Miami Heat on a two-year, $13 million deal with a player option in the second year once he clears waivers, providing some much-needed shooting around Giannis Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo on the new-look Heat. Thompson, 36, signed with the Mavericks in 2024 and played 141 games in Dallas, averaging 12.9 points on 40.3/38.7/85.1 shooting splits in two seasons. With Dallas pivoting toward a youth movement led by reigning Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg, the Mavericks had little need to keep Thompson on the roster for the 2026-27 season and opted to reach a buyout well before training camp began to give him the opportunity to sign with a contender. "Klay is one of the great players and competitors of his generation, and we are grateful for everything he brought to the Mavericks organization," Mavericks president of basketball operations Masai Ujiri said in a statement. "We have tremendous respect for Klay and all that he has accomplished throughout his career, and we wish him nothing but the best moving forward."
Thompson clearly already had his preferred destination in mind when negotiating a buyout with the Mavs, with word he planned to join the Heat coming mere minutes after the news went public. While Thompson isn't the two-way force he was at his peak, his shooting acumen is something the Heat desperately need on their roster after trading Tyler Herro to Milwaukee and letting Norman Powell walk in free agency to bring in Antetokounmpo. 
        
            
                Ranking the NBA's 12 best duos: Three new-look pairs make the list, but familiar names are at the top
                
                    John Gonzalez                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Miami faced hard cap restrictions in building out its roster around Antetokounmpo and Adebayo, and hoped to accelerate its timeline as a contender by signing LeBron James. Once James opted to join the Philadelphia 76ers, the Heat had to pivot to find veteran reinforcements for the roster and landed a four-time NBA champion in Thompson to bolster their pursuit of a fourth title in Miami. Thompson will join Andrew Wiggins, Nikola Jovic, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Dru Smith as Miami's wing rotation, providing coach Erik Spoelstra with another option for building lineups around their All-Star frontcourt. 
Thompson's shooting efficiency has dipped a bit from his peak since returning from ACL and Achilles injuries, but in the five seasons since getting back on the court, he's still shot 39.3% from three on 8.8 attempts per game. Given how few shooters Miami has on its roster, Thompson figures to find a prominent role in the Heat's rotation as they look to climb back into the upper echelon of the Eastern Conference.

title: DeMar DeRozan signing with Nuggets: How does he fit with Nikola Jokić, Jamal Murray? - CBS Sports
description: Denver is coming off a first-round playoff exit and hoping to keep pace in a competitive Western Conference
body:
Denver is coming off a first-round playoff exit and hoping to keep pace in a competitive Western Conference

        DeMar DeRozan will play his 18th NBA season with the Denver Nuggets after agreeing to a one-year, minimum deal, per multiple reports. The veteran wing will join Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray in Denver to help fill the void at forward after the Nuggets dealt restricted free agent Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers in a sign-and-trade earlier this week. DeRozan, 37, played the last two seasons with the Sacramento Kings, averaging 20.3 points, 4.3 assists and 3.4 rebounds per game on 48.6/32.5/86.2 shooting splits. The Kings waived DeRozan earlier this offseason, making him a free agent. The Nuggets, coming off a first-round playoff exit, will hope that DeRozan, Cameron Johnson and Aaron Gordon can provide a strong wing rotation between Jokić and Murray.DeRozan will provide them with another scoring option and on-ball creator on the roster, but the fit with this particular Nuggets core isn't the cleanest on paper.  
For one, DeRozan's weakness as an offensive player has always been his 3-point shooting, and Denver's offense has leaned heavily on its wings to provide space on the perimeter for the Jokić-Murray two-man game to thrive. Watson shot 41.1% on 3s last year. DeRozan shot 32.5% from beyond the arc, but the majority of his shots came from the midrange. 
        
            
                The Nuggets are daring Nikola Jokić to leave after a listless summer
                
                    Brad Botkin                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
From there, Denver's offense is heavily predicated on Jokić's creation abilities and the rest of the offense following his lead. DeRozan did play more off the ball in Sacramento, but still self-created more than 61% of his 2-point baskets with the Kings. Watson, on the other hand, was assisted on 65.2% of his 2-point baskets last season, and how the Nuggets balance the contrasting styles will be fascinating to watch. The optimistic view is that DeRozan can help helm the bench unit that has long been an Achilles heel of the Nuggets during Jokić's tenure. DeRozan's abilities as a tough shotmaker might not be ideal in Jokić-led lineups, where the Nuggets can create better opportunities than DeRozan's typical shot diet. But when the three-time MVP is off the floor, DeRozan becomes far more valuable. 
How coach David Adelman deploys DeRozan in the rotation and how well DeRozan adapts to playing alongside Jokić will determine the level of success Denver can have in 2026-27. Gordon is a prime example of a player who embraced the positives of a smaller creative role alongside Jokić and has thrived, but not everyone is capable of making that adjustment, particularly a player who has had as much individual success as DeRozan. Nuggets fans are already a bit on edge about how the franchise is handling roster building during Jokić's prime years, with the Watson trade raising concerns about their commitment to fully investing in trying to win another championship with arguably the league's best player. DeRozan will, fairly or not, bear some of the weight of expectations to help keep Denver in the contender tier in the West with the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder, even on a minimum contract.

The 30-year-old began his career with the Cleveland Browns after being drafted 35th overall in the second round of the 2018 NFL Draft out of Georgia. Chubb reeled off four consecutive 1,000-yard rushing seasons from 2019 to 2022, which earned him four consecutive Pro Bowl selections. His best year came in 2022 with a career-high 1,525 yards rushing to go along with a career-high 12 rushing touchdowns. That production earned him second-team All-Pro honors. The 2023 season is when injuries began to rob him of his prime years. He tore both his MCL, meniscus and ACL in 2023 after a gruesome knee injury against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 2 that year.  Chubb returned to action in Week 7 of the 2024 season before suffering another season-ending injury in Week 15 that year against the Kansas City Chiefs, this time a foot fracture. He was a shell of himself in 2025 with the Houston Texans after the second, significant lower body injury as he rushed for just 506 yards and 3 touchdowns on 122 carries. That's why he called it quits while remaining a free agent two weeks into the 2026 preseason. "Today's the day I've been avoiding for a while," Chubb wrote. "Twelve-year-old me could never imagine this day, and 30-year-old me is wondering where all the time has gone. I've known for some time now, but I'm finally ready to share that I'm done playing football. I wanted to end my career on a healthy note, along with a winning season, and I was able to do that. At the beginning of this journey, I made many promises to myself. The No. 1 promise I made was that I would always stay true to who I am and forget the things that made me, me. That promise meant always being the hardest-working person, not whether where I was or what the circumstances were."

Chubb's peak of his first five seasons from 2018 to 2022 stands almost without equal in NFL history after he registered 6,341 yards rushing on a 5.2 yards per carry average. He and Pro Football Hall of Famer Jim Brown are the only players in league history with 6,000-plus rushing yards and 5-plus yards per carry in their first five seasons, per CBS Sports Research. Chubb's sixth season in 2023 is when his career-altering knee injury occurred. 
"In the NFL, I wanted to lead the league in rushing, win MVP and win a Super Bowl for the city of Cleveland," Chubb said. "I wasn't able to accomplish any of those things. ... What's most frustrating but also gives me peace is that I know for a fact I gave it my all."

title: Inside the fastest show in baseball: What it's like to watch Brewers sensation Jacob Misiorowski - CBS Sports
description: MILWAUKEE – The greatest show on the sand, silt, and clay of the pitcher's mound these days is Milwaukee Brewers right-handed force of n
body:
MILWAUKEE – The greatest show on the sand, silt, and clay of the pitcher's mound these days is Milwaukee Brewers right-handed force of nature Jacob Misiorowski. The 24-year-old is not just the best pitcher in the world in 2026, he's also the most viscerally overwhelming pitcher in the world. Misiorowski on Friday at the Brewers' home yard squared off against Chris Sale, one of the best at his craft and a pitcher some 13 years Misiorowski's senior. It was not only a clash of aces, it was also a duel between two of the best teams in baseball. The 40,130 in attendance -- marking the 16th Milwaukee sell-out of the season (and this one on weekday afternoon) – surely knew it meant a little more than most August games do.  Beyond the importance of the outcome -- Milwaukee won 2-1 -- and what it meant to a Brewers team trying to fend off the Cubs and secure top seed throughout the postseason and a Braves team angling to secure a bye, it was a Misiorowski start. No matter the opponent, that's appointment viewing these days. If you were watching, here's what you saw. First inningWorking from the first base side of the rubber, Misiorowski opens with a 101.8 mph fastball to greet Braves leadoff hitter Ronald Acuña Jr. It's a ball inside. Misiorowski will go to the fastball with all five pitches that Acuña sees -- all triple digits, and four of them out of the zone. Acuña flicks away the only strike, one on the outside sliver of the zone, and works a walk. 
With most starting pitchers, we'd note that they'd now be working from the stretch. Misirowski, though, is unusual among starting pitchers in that he always works from the stretch. Perhaps, with his long levers and maxed-out stuff, keeping it simple is the soundest approach. It's certainly impossible to argue with the results, just as it's impossible to argue with the Brewers' faculties when it comes to pitching development. On Misiorowski's sixth pitch of the game, he finally departs from the fastball and presents Drake Baldwin with a 98-mph cutter. Two offerings later, he goes to the slider for the first time on Friday. It's not his fully gassed-up slider. He's touched 98 with his slider this season, although when his slide-piece is at those levels, it might be more of a cutter than a true slider. If you call it a true slider, then Misiorowski has thrown 49 of the 50 fastest sliders on record. Is a 98-mph slider more impressive than his occasional 104-mph fastball? It might be, if, of course, it's a slider in the genuine sense and not a cutter or the infelicitously named slutter. We know that his fastball is a fastball, though, so it's fine to direct your amazement there, as you likely already were. Misiorowski gets his first strikeout of the game on a 101.6 mph fastball that catches the outside edge at Baldwin's expense. 
Speaking of the typical purpose of pitching from the stretch -- to hold runners -- preventing the steal is a skill of Misiorowski's that gets overlooked. On that note: This was a delayed steal on the part of Acuña, so the out was more an instance of poor decision-making running headlong into William Contreras' powerful throwing arm. Contreras is among the game's best when it comes to controlling the running game, but let's note that Misiorowski has allowed only one stolen base this season – the fewest among qualifiers alongside Ryan Weathers.  Not long after, Misiorowski ends the frame with a backfoot slider to Matt Olson that he whiffs on. He throws the slider about three times as often to right-handed batters, but, as Olson will surely attest, he can back-foot it to left-handed batters as a putaway pitch. This one was 91.8 mph, so, yes, it's a true slider. 
Second inningIt seems like the merest matter of time before Misiorowski eventually authors a no-hitter, but it won't be today. With two out, Mauricio Dubón lines an 0-2 fastball to right for a single. At 103.1 mph, the pitch is Misiorowski's hastiest of the day and the first pitch we've seen enter what's informally known as "Miz Velo Country." It's not particularly fair to throw that hard as a starting pitcher, and what makes it even less fair from the Misiorowski standpoint is how close to the plate he releases the ball. The 6-foot-7 Misiorowski gets, on average, an absurd 7.6 feet of extension off the rubber and toward the plate. That puts him in the 99th percentile in extension among big league hurlers. Take a look at Misiorowski's first inning landing spot, as amateurishly captured from the American Family Field press box: 
And here's how it looked in the fourth inning after Sale has put his spikes on the mound: As you can see, the 6-foot-6 Sale had been planting well behind Misirowski. Sale gets his six-and-a-half feet in extension, on average, and that puts him in the 59th percentile, but thanks to his crossfire delivery he doesn't get down the hill as much as Misiorowski does. That's where the notion of effective velocity comes into play. The hitter obviously has vanishingly little time to react to Misiorowski's fastball, and because he releases the ball so close to the hitter, it's even less time than you might think. Misiorowski this season has averaged 100.6 mph with his fastball, but his average effective velocity -- meaning what the pitch feels like to the hitter -- is 103.1 mph thanks to his elite extension. He has a high leg lift, with the knee basically coming in line with the jersey lettering when he's going into his delivery, and that sets him up to stride deep toward the plate. 
When we talk about Miz's fastball, we'll often couch it in terms like "fastest by a starting pitcher" when talking about Aroldis Chapman in historical terms or Mason Miller on the contemporary front. Miller indeed does best Misiorowski on the radar gun, with an average four-seamer of 101.5 mph. In effective velocity, though, Miller comes in at 102.4 mph because he gets less extension than Misiorowski. Miller may throw harder, but most hitters would probably tell you that Miz seems like he throws hardest of all.  He induced a 2-1 fly-out from Dom Smith to strand Dubón and end the inning. Third inningThe third frame, in which after the first two batters Misiorowski gets into the Atlanta lineup for the second time, sees him take a slider-heavy approach. Of his 11 pitches in the inning, just three are fastballs. He goes to the four-seamer more than 60% of the time overall, which is a point of distinction these days, so this is a brief departure for Misiorowski. Like most teams, the Braves are less effective against breaking stuff than fastballs, and Misiorowski is getting deeper into his secondaries a bit early, since he probably won't go extremely deep into this game even if the zeroes continue to stack up. He's pitching on extra rest, as is custom with him lately, as his workload continues to mount and as the Brewers increasingly operate with a focus on a deep October run. Misiorowski whiffs Austin Riley on a fastball after feeding him three straight sliders. Against the Braves No. 9 hitter, Mike Yastrzemski, he throws a curve for the first time. The curve is actually Miz's best pitch in terms of whiff rate, but this one lands a bit too middle-in, and Yastrzemski lines it to right for a single. First pitch ground-outs to Acuña and Baldwin end the frame. 
Fourth inningFreshly staked to a 2-0 lead, Misirowski benefits from the first ABS challenge of the day by Contreras, who flips a called ball into a called strike at the top of the zone to put Olson in an 0-1 count. He's back to a fastball-heavy approach in this inning and throws three straight balls to Olson before retiring him on back-to-back swinging strikes at the fastball. With a 2-1 count, Harris stings a 99.7 mph high fastball – it's the first hard-hit ball that Misiorowski has permitted on this day – but center fielder Luis Lara makes a nifty ranging catch to prevent extra bases. The 16-pitch perfect frame ends on an Ozzie Albies fly-out. Fifth inningFor a pitcher like Misiorowski, who doesn't throw a sinker and leans so heavily on a four-seamer he likes to spot high in the zone, you wouldn't expect strong groundball tendencies. But Misiorowski has a ground-ball percentage of 45.1, which puts him in the 64th percentile among MLB hurlers. This is because his secondaries all get more grounders than you'd expect given their traits and types. The fifth provides a reminder, and Dubón leads off the inning by grounding out to Brice Turang at second on a Miz cutter. The pitch was at the very top of the zone, but because of the late natural sink it dipped under the barrel and registered a -3 degree launch angle. Another ground ball followed, but this one off the bat of Smith (with a -17 degree launch angle) sneaked into right field for a hit. Facing Riley for the second time, Misiorowski flipped his approach and went fastballs broken up by a slider. He earned a whiff. The Braves brought the potential tying run to the plate when Yastrzemski earned a four-pitch walk -- not a common occurrence for Misiorowski. Yes, his stuff is electricity set on fire, but it's all harnessed and commanded. He's walked just 6% of opposing batters, which is figure that puts him among the league's top control artists (a descriptor that, even so, will never be applied to him). This walk meant Misiorowski would face the perilous Acuña for the third time on Friday in a crucial spot. With a 1-2 count, he fed the former MVP a fastball above the zone followed by a slider at the very bottom of it. One -17 degree launch angle later, a 6-3 putout ended the threat. 
Sixth inningImprobably, Misiorowski this season has permitted a .122/.230/.194 line when facing an opposing lineup for the third time in a start. Still, in-game familiarity benefits the hitter, and the theory holds even when a pitcher like Misiorowski is defying it. The sixth indeed occasioned danger for the Milwaukee ace. To start, he freezes Baldwin for a punchout on the sixth pitch of their encounter. Next was Olson, and Misiorowski got ahead 0-2 thanks to two different brands of sliders – one back door and one back foot. Olson evens the count at 2-2 and then bruises a high fastball, 104.8 mph off the bat, to center. Lara, though, is on the case: The ball off Olson's bat had an expected batting average of .770, but in truth that figure turned out to be .000. Two pitches later, Harris smoked a double to right off a slider, and a mound visit followed. An Albies fly-out put an end to the inning. With a pitch count of 96 Misiorowski's day was probably already done, but the Brewers no doubt noted that against Albies he threw his slowest four-seamer at 97.2 mph and his slowest cutter at 94.7 mph. The Fatigued state is when mechanics go awry, and we know what can happen from there. Wielding the beast of unthinkable velocity means respecting it, at least if you want to keep wielding it. He wasn't his sharpest self in that inning, and, who can say, if the sunlight didn't break through that bank of windows at American Family Field in the sixth and complicate the hitting visuals, maybe it's not a spotless day after all for Misiorowski. 
His final line: 
As of that work, Misiorowski this season has an ERA of 1.68 and an FIP of 2.14 in 145 innings. He's also struck out 216 batters, which comes to a K% of 39.3 -- an absurd figure for any pitcher, let alone a starter who isn't even a quarter-century old yet. All of that -- everything, really -- leads the majors.   The Braves broke through against the Milwaukee bullpen with a run in the eighth and put the tying run on base in the ninth, but in the end the crisp two-hour and 21-minute pitcher's duel -- connoisseur's baseball -- went the way most expected it to. It went to the better team and -- this is often said in reference to a probable future Hall of Famer like Sale -- the better pitcher. The Brewers, thanks to the heavy lifting of Misiorowski, are now the first team to 80 wins in 2026. Given the two moundsmen involved and the two teams involved, it all felt like a prelude to something bigger, say, seven or eight weeks from now. That sounds all right, does it not?

        Selecting elite fantasy blueliners can go a long way to creating a well-balanced roster. Beyond the cream of the crop, which consists of defensemen proficient enough to produce points on par with upper-level top-six forwards, there are numerous viable options for managers seeking versatility across multiple categories. While this is not meant to be used as an exact order for drafting, it can serve as a helpful tool to identify groupings of rearguards to choose from, what to expect from them and a rough idea of when they could be targeted.  Tier 1 - Best of the BestCale Makar Makar remains in a class of his own due to his offensive ability. He is capable of making an impact every time he hops onto the ice and has reached the 90-point plateau in two of the past three campaigns. He also racks up power-play points, shots and blocks. Makar remains the lone blueliner worthy of being a top-10 fantasy selection. Tier 2 - Best of the RestEvan Bouchard, Quinn Hughes, Zach Werenski They are all elite offensive contributors capable of producing points at a point-per-game rate while logging heavy minutes. Bouchard and Hughes see time on excellent power-play units, while Werenski has been the best even-strength producer among all blueliners over the last three regular seasons. Fantasy managers fortunate enough to choose one of them should feel confident their defense is set for the season. 
Tier 3 - Elite Multi-Category Building Blocks Lane Hutson, Rasmus Dahlin, Moritz Seider, Matthew Schaefer, Adam Fox, Jackson LaCombe, Miro Heiskanen The skaters in this grouping record outstanding offensive statistics while adding solid shot, block and power-play totals. Dahlin and Seider are also great sources of hits. It didn't take long for Hutson and Schaefer to establish themselves as impact fantasy options, while LaCombe still has room to grow following his breakout performance in 2025-26.Tier 4 - High-End OptionsDarren Raddysh, Josh Morrissey, Jake Sanderson, Roman Josi, Mikhail Sergachev, Erik Karlsson, Charlie McAvoy, Shayne Gostisbehere, Shea Theodore, Jakob Chychrun, John Carlson, Brock Faber
They all possess superb offensive skills and are likely to see plenty of power-play time in the 2026-27 season. They will also chip in shots, blocks and hits, making them solid options for fantasy managers who are unwilling to invest higher draft capital in a rearguard but still want a reliable primary alternative. Tier 5 - Taking the Next Step Brandt Clarke, Bowen Byram, Alexander Nikishin, Luke Hughes, Simon Nemec, Philip BrobergThese defenders could provide plenty of bang for the buck if they reach their potential in the 2026-27 campaign. With the exception of Nikishin (unless he is traded), they all should be in line for increased roles and could provide strong category coverage. However, Clarke could be held back by Drew Doughty, while Dougie Hamilton may stunt the progress of Hughes.
Tier 6 - Well-Rounded Depth Pieces Noah Dobson, Thomas Harley, Rasmus Andersson, Dougie Hamilton, Victor Hedman, Seth Jones, Thomas Chabot, Brandon Montour, K'Andre Miller, Noah Hanifin, Neal Pionk, Sean Durzi, Vince Dunn, Filip Hronek, Devon Toews, Ivan Provorov, Mattias Ekholm, Esa Lindell, Morgan Rielly, Aaron Ekblad, Vladislav Gavrikov, Travis Sanheim, Kris Letang, Dmitry OrlovWhile several of them have had some recent injury issues, they remain solid depth options for potential fantasy managers. They can supply offense, shots, blocks, hits and power-play points for a decent mix of value. Under the right circumstances, they could surpass the 40-point plateau and push for 50. Tier 7 - Well-Rounded, but with Concerns Jacob Trouba, Olen Zellweger, Mattias Samuelsson, MacKenzie Weegar, Darnell Nurse, Simon Edvinsson, Sean Walker, Sam Malinski, Drew Doughty, Cam Fowler, Jamie Drysdale 
This grouping isn't far from the previous one, but there are some question marks and their offensive ceiling isn't as high. Nurse, Zellweger and Trouba will be occupying new roles with different teams this season, while Edvinsson, Weegar, Doughty and Fowler regressed in 2025-26. Samuelsson, Walker, Malinski and Drysdale may struggle to repeat their respective breakout efforts from last campaign. Tier 8 - Bursting with Potential  Cole Hutson, Zeev Buium, Zayne Parekh, Sam Rinzel, Artyom Levshunov, Logan Mailloux, Carter Yakemchuk, Luca Cagnoni Hutson, Yakemchuk and Cagnoni could be intriguing fantasy options this season if they secure NHL lineup spots, especially if they land prominent power-play time. Buium, Parekh and Mailloux should continue to see their roles expand in 2026-27. The arrival of Byram hurts the potential of Rinzel and Levshunov, but Chicago's young blue line is worth monitoring for all-round upside. 
Tier 9 - Physical, Banger-League Possibilities  Nikita Zadorov, Brenden Dillon, Braden Schneider, Ben Chiarot, Jeremy Lauzon, Radko Gudas, Connor Clifton, Jake McCabe, Martin Fehervary, Adam Larsson, Nick Seeler, Matt Roy, Brayden McNabb, Zach Whitecloud, Colton Parayko, Rasmus Ristolainen Most of the options here won't provide many points, but they can compile 100-plus hits and 100-plus blocks. They will also probably end up with a healthy amount of penalty minutes. Lauzon leads the league in hits over the past three seasons, while Gudas ranks second. McCabe was the league leader in blocked shots in the 2025-26 regular season.

        Gauging what to make of programs with new coaches is particularly challenging in the modern age of college football, when rosters can be flipped in a span of weeks with a quick wave of the portal wand. We've seen previously unfathomable one-year turnarounds at schools like Indiana, followed by monumental first-year flops at schools like North Carolina.If you're willing to look under the hood and dissect the nuances of each situation, there is value to be found from a betting perspective with new regimes. A year ago, Wake Forest's over on a 4.5 win total was priced at +116, and it hit before the end of October as the Demon Deacons rode a favorable schedule to an 8-4 mark under first-year coach Jake Dickert.That was among the five bets included in this column, which is now in its fifth year. Four of them hit, as my four-year record on win totals improved to 15-3 with five pushes. This year, we are returning to the first-year coach vein for three of our five selections.
        
            
                College football win totals: Eight teams poised for big rise or fall in number of victories in 2026
                
                    Chris Hummer                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The first season is not always an indicator of a coach's future viability for a variety of reasons. Wildly imbalanced conference schedules are a major swing factor, and that's a large part of the rationale for my faith in Penn State. New coach Matt Campbell's learning curve will be made simpler by the absence of three Big Ten heavyweights from the Nittany Lions' 2026 schedule.
My degree of confidence in these is high, and a 3-2 record with these odds is guaranteed to break even. If you want to go bold and take Arkansas to go under 3.5 and/or go with Minnesota over 6.5, the payout could be even better. Here are the 2026 season's best bets, with odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Penn State: Over 9.5 wins (+140)A schedule that misses Indiana, Ohio State and Oregon will ease Matt Campbell's transition from Iowa State to Penn State. The Nittany Lions' nonconference slate of Marshall, Temple and Buffalo is also light, and five of Penn State's nine league games are at home. Campbell's Iowa State-heavy transfer class is the No. 4-ranked haul in the country, and a nice sampling of talent from the James Franklin era is still around. Among them are a star left tackle in Anthony Donkoh, a veteran leader at linebacker in Tony Rojas and a proven starter at corner in Audavion Collins. All told, the conditions are optimized for the Nittany Lions to win 10 or 11 regular-season games and crack the CFP in Year 1 of the new regime. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Minnesota: Over 5.5 wins (-160)Minnesota's rushing offense is mired in an uncharacteristic lull that should end in 2026 behind an offensive line that features an NFL Draft prospect at guard in Greg Johnson and a 2025 freshman All-American at tackle in Nathan Roy. Furthermore, Drake Lindsey is back at quarterback after a promising redshirt freshman campaign. He should only improve when defenses have to respect the Gophers' rushing attack again. Minnesota also misses Ohio State and Oregon, leaving an Oct. 31 game at Indiana as the only contest that looks outright unwinnable. Even when you write in losses against Michigan, at Indiana and at Penn State, the Gophers still have plenty of wiggle room to reach six wins. If you're a big believer, taking the over 6.5 will bring a significantly better payout.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Arkansas under 4.5 (-200)First-year coach Ryan Silverfield is due for a rude welcome to the SEC. Not only is he arriving just as the league goes to a nine-game conference schedule, but the Razorbacks also face a Week 2 road trip to play Utah. As the school's administration has pointed out with great ire, that late-night contest (at altitude) will be followed by a noon Eastern kick against Georgia the following week. The hits keep coming with trips to Texas A&M and Texas, along with tricky home games against established programs like Tennessee and Missouri. A second straight 2-10 campaign is possible. But even if the Razorbacks pull a couple of league upsets, it's hard to fathom a universe in which they reach 5-7 with a totally overhauled roster featuring inexperienced quarterback options. The under 3.5 comes with a significantly better payout and should also be considered by those with bullish tastes.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Iowa State: under 5.5 (-220)After Matt Campbell's 3-9 debut in 2016, the Cyclones only failed to reach six regular-season victories once in his next nine years, creating an impression that perhaps Iowa State had leveled up its floor. But as the program reboots under Jimmy Rogers, a bottoming out could be in store. This is a total scrape-and-rebuild. While Rogers is bringing 15 players with him from Washington State, he was only there for a single 7-6 season. It's not as if the bedrock of an established program is arriving, as we often see with other first-year coaches. While the Big 12 schedule isn't brutal -- the Cyclones miss Texas Tech and Houston -- Iowa State will likely need to win four conference games to cash the over. It's hard to see this ISU roster grinding out four league wins in Year 1 with the nation's 67th-ranked transfer class. 
                            
    
                                                
                    
    BYU over 8.5 (-150)Of the other three Big 12 teams that reached double-digit victories last season, BYU only has to play one as part of a schedule featuring five Big 12 home games. There is no Texas Tech on the slate and no Houston. The toughest road game is a quick bus ride down I-15 to play rival Utah, which is in the midst of a coaching transition. With key playmakers back throughout the defense, the only real question is who will emerge to catch passes from star sophomore quarterback Bear Bachmeier. He's got 1,300-yard rusher LJ Martin back, and the Cougars are poised to field another group of maulers on the offensive line. This program is absolutely humming under Kalani Sitake and should reach double-digit victories for a third straight season. If you're a big believer, find over 9.5 for a better return.

There will be practice on either Thursday or Friday, with a qualifying event to set up the grid on either Friday or Saturday depending on the race schedule. Qualifying usually takes place the day before the race. Bettors can wager on qualifying outcomes as well, and those results will shift the race odds.Biggest races for motor sports bettingArguably, the biggest sporting event in the racing world is the Indianapolis 500, which is traditionally held on Memorial Day weekend. That's the premier IndyCar event.NASCAR has several big races, with the Daytona 500, a Crown Jewel event, regarded as the richest race on the circuit. The Coca-Cola 600 at Charlotte and the Brickyard 400 are also considered Crown Jewel events. Talladega Speedway is a widely known track thanks to the movie "Talladega Nights: The Ballad of Ricky Bobby", but it is not a Crown Jewel event.Every F1 race has its unique twist. The tracks are different in each city, but Monaco is considered the biggest spectacle of the season. The race itself is somewhat mundane because there's little opportunity for drivers to pass each other. The British Grand Prix at Silverstone, the Italian Grand Prix at Monza and the Singapore Grand Prix are considered some marquee events on the F1 calendar. The Abu Dhabi Grand Prix is also a high-profile event as it is typically last on the calendar and could decide who wins the drivers championship and constructors championship. F1 has also added special events like Miami and Las Vegas.Types of bets and how motor sports betting works Like all sports betting markets, there are a variety of ways prospective bettors can wager on motor sports. Here's a look at some of them.Outright/To Win oddsThis market is straightforward. Users are betting on which driver will win the event. There are also markets here for which team/constructor car will win the event, which will have multiple cars involved.Placement/Top Finish oddsMotor sports betting offers users the ability to wager on drivers or teams having a certain placement or finishing within a certain range. For example, you can wager on drivers to place in the top 5 or top 10 of the event. You can do the same with teams/constructors.While it rarely occurs in racing, there's a possibility of multiple drivers tying for a position. In this case, there are  technically multiple winning bets. However, sportsbooks grade dead heats differently and the payouts can be different. If FanDuel declares a dead heat, half the stake is applied at the original odds and half the stake is lost. If there are more than two dead heats, the stakes are proportioned accordingly.Dual ForecastThis is where bettors can place a wager on which drivers will finish first and second. Both drivers must finish in the correct order for this wager to be paid out as a win. For example, you can wager on Max Verstappen and Lando Norris to finish first and second, respectively in a Dual Forecast market in F1 betting. However, if Verstappen finishes second and Norris finishes first, your bet will lose even though you did correctly pick the top two drivers for the race.Each Way BettingThis is not as common in motor sports but can be applied to racing betting. An each way bet basically places two wagers: a driver to win and to finish above another position. If the driver wins, both bets get paid out. The same applies for team bets in this market.Stage WinnerThis is prevalent in NASCAR and IndyCar, which has more laps than Formula One. You can bet on which driver or team will be in the lead after 25 laps, 50 laps, 100 laps and so on. These are the stages.Matchups/Head-to-HeadSportsbooks will put two drivers or two teams against each other, allowing bettors to choose which one will place higher. For teams, the bet is usually on the highest-placed driver for that particular team. This is one of the more popular F1 betting strategies. For example, if a market was being offered on F1 to see if Ferrari or Mercedes placed higher, the highest-placing Ferrari driver determines the result, even if both Mercedes drivers finish ahead of the second Ferrari driver. This means that bettors must consider both driver and car in situations like this.Group WinnerThis is offered in NASCAR. Sportsbooks will put a handful of drivers in groups and ask which will be the winner of the group.Top Car Make DriverThis is also specific to NASCAR, where you can bet on whether the winning driver will be in a particular car manufacturer, like Ford or Chevy. It's more applicable here since there are only two drivers on each F1 constructor, while car brands can span several NASCAR teams.Team of Race WinnerThis is similar to Outright Winner for drivers but applies to teams and constructors.Qualifying BetsBettors can wager on who will take pole position and which cars will be on pole. These are determined during qualifying racing, which typically takes place the day before the race. You can also bet on markets offering odds for who will finish in the top 5 or top 10 in qualifying, though these aren't necessarily  available for every race. The results of qualifying will often shift the race odds.Motor sports futures bettingFormula 1 bettingIn most cases, F1 futures usually apply to the next race. However, you can bet on season-long futures for F1 championship betting. The Drivers Championship is straightforward as it will be given to the driver who accumulates the most points over the season. The Constructors Championship takes into account the points for both team drivers. Only the top 10 finishers in each race score points, and those points are tallied over the season. The winning driver can be part of a constructors championship, but that's not always the case.Here are the latest odds for the F1 Dutch GP 2026, which begins August 21st. Odds were last updated on August 21 and are courtesy of FanDuel Sportsbook.Andrea Kimi Antonelli +180Lando Norris +215George Russell +550Lewis Hamilton +800Charles Leclerc +800Oscar Piastri +1000NASCAR BettingNASCAR has different portions of the season. There are also different circuits like the Cup Series, the Xfinity Series and Truck Series. You can bet on marquee races for NASCAR in the futures market, and you can also wager on winners for these particular series.As of August 21, 2026, here are the latest odds to win the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Dollar Tree 301, per DraftKings Sportsbook:Ryan Blaney +450Christopher Bell +500Joey Logano +550Denny Hamlin +600Chase Briscoe +850IndyCarThe major marquee futures market for IndyCar is the Indianapolis 500. Other than that race, there are season-long championship odds for the circuit.Can you parlay wagers in motor sports betting?While parlaying is generally not advised, as you don't get appropriate odds from sportsbooks that correspond to the actual chance of your bet winning, you are able to parlay outcomes in motor sports betting. While you can't pick multiple drivers to win an event in a parlay, you can pick multiple drivers to finish in the top 5 or top 10. You can also pick teams to finish in the top 5 or top 10.How to bet on motor sports live during a raceSportsbooks do offer live odds for motor sports, though this is likely a more prominent feature for NASCAR and IndyCar as opposed to F1. Driver and team odds will shift based on where they are in the grand scheme of the race. NASCAR and IndyCar allow for more leeway since there are more laps, while F1 can sometimes shift quickly towards one driver or team.Tips and strategies for how to bet on motor sportsDriver form does matter when it comes to racing, but the biggest predictor of success is usually how each team can adjust to conditions. Races can take place in all kinds of weather and team strategy can make or break the day. There are some teams that struggle to adjust, and bettors should know which teams those are before placing wagers. Historical track success often takes a back seat to current form. For example, Max Verstappen won the Canadian Grand Prix three years in a row and was a contender after starting second behind George Russell in 2025. Russell has had mixed results in Montreal historically but wound up winning the race after winning qualifying to take pole position.Longshots obviously don't usually win races, so they are better served as an inclusion in placement markets. You can usually back drivers who have had success on certain tracks or who have routinely finished just outside of a certain position market to break through eventually.Occasionally, a caution flag comes out when there's a crash on the track, which makes racing conditions hazardous for everyone. When this happens, there will be a safety car deployed, and all drivers must line up behind the safety car until the wreck is managed. There are different rules for each association and sometimes the race organizer makes a call in the moment, but usually, the race cannot end on a caution flag. If the wreck is too big to clear in a reasonable amount of time, the race will end despite the caution flag being signaled. Overtime doesn't really exist, but usually there will be at least one additional lap of racing should the fallout of the crash get removed in a timely manner and the safety car gets taken off the track.FAQCan you bet on motor sports?As long as you are of legal age in a state where sports betting is legitimate, you should be able to find a sportsbook which provides racing and motor sports odds.Who to bet on for the Indy 500?Because the Indy 500 typically takes place over Memorial Day weekend, you'll have to wait for a bit before placing wagers on who will win the signature event. Josef Newgarden won the Indy 500 in 2023 and 2024 but Alex Palou won in 2025 and is the reigning champion.Can you bet on SuperCross?SuperCross is a type of motorcycle racing. Some sportsbooks do offer SuperCross odds in certain states.Can you bet on motocross at DraftKings?DraftKings does provide SuperCross odds, which is a motocross competition, in select states. You must be of legal age and residing in those states to bet on motocross at DraftKings.How to bet on F1?All major sportsbooks have lines available for F1 races. title: Arsenal vs. Coventry City live stream: Where to watch Premier League online - CBS Sports
description: Arsenal enter the season as defending champions and will kicking things off against newly promoted side Coventry
body:
Arsenal enter the season as defending champions and will kicking things off against newly promoted side Coventry City, which marks the first game of the new campaign
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:15 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
No two Premier League seasons are ever exactly alike but as a new one begins this weekend, there is an unusually unpredictable – and exciting – feeling to this one.Most of the league's 20 teams enter the new campaign in some form of transition, be it through new managers, squad turnover or the task of successfully making the jump from the Championship to the top flight. Naturally, a few constants still hold true. Reigning champions Arsenal remain mostly unchanged from last season's triumphs and, after several years of continuity, look to repeat as title winners. The promoted trio of Coventry City, Ipswich Town and Hull City will also have their work cut out for them, the odds of staying up not exactly in their favor. Everything else, though, is up in the air.The opening round of games will offer a first real glimpse at the many, many teams who return to play with new plans, while the early weeks of the season will help fill in the gaps as onlookers begin to learn each team's new patterns. That said, several key matchups will be particularly revealing. Manchester City, now without ex-coach Pep Guardiola and midfielder Rodri, will take on a Bournemouth side under new management of their own but eager to build upon last season's results that saw them qualify for European competition for the first time. Chelsea's clash with Fulham, meanwhile, marks a meeting between last season's Real Madrid managers – Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa, each with a different point to prove.The new season opens on Friday with a battle between England's most recent champions, Arsenal and Championship winners Coventry City.Here's what you need to know as a new season begins.Premier League opening weekend scheduleAll times U.S./EsternFriday, Aug. 21Arsenal vs. Coventry City, 3 p.m. (USA Network)Saturday, Aug. 22Hull City vs. Manchester United, 7:30 a.m. (USA Network)Everton vs. Crystal Palace, 10 a.m. (USA Network)Ipswich Town vs. Sunderland, 10 a.m. (Peacock)Nottingham Forest vs. Leeds United, 10 a.m. (Peacock)Brentford vs. Tottenham Hotspur, 12:30 p.m. (Peacock)Sunday, Aug. 23Manchester City vs. Bournemouth, 9 a.m. (USA Network)Brighton and Hove Albion vs. Aston Villa, 9 a.m. (Peacock)Newcastle United vs. Liverpool, 11:30 a.m. (USA Network)Monday, Aug. 24Fulham vs. Chelsea, 3 p.m. (USA Network)New managers everywhere you lookNine teams enter the new season with new managers, while Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur begin the new campaign with coaches who are in their first full seasons in charge. It leaves a lot of entertaining uncertainty in every section of the table, but most intriguing at the top end. The Gunners would have gone in as the favorites to repeat as champions regardless of what their opponents got up to over the summer but at this point of the season, it's hard to know who – if any – will mount a reasonable challenge. The questions facing each of them are meaty, too. Will Enzo Maresca be able to transition smoothly into his new role at City after Pep Guardiola's storied decade in charge? Can Xabi Alonso steer Chelsea in the right direction after years of ups and downs under the new owners – and put the chaos of Real Madrid behind him? Will Andoni Iraola find a way to get Liverpool's high-profile attacking unit going after last summer's spending spree? Are Manchester United normal now?Can the promoted teams stay up?Even amidst a sea of change in the Premier League, some things always stay the same. That includes the grueling fight for survival for the teams who earned promotion from the Championship, none of which seem well-equipped to stay up. Despite being one of the Championship's worst defensive teams last season, Hull City rode their luck to Wembley Stadium and managed to win the promotion playoff but seem poised for a rude awakening in the Premier League. Ipswich Town have made some signings they hope will turn good and like many other colleagues, have a new manager in Gary O'Neill who has a track record of leading teams to punch above their own weight, but a lot will have to go right for them to survive. The team perhaps best positioned to stay up is Coventry City, though they will miss goalscorer Haji Wright for the start of the season – the U.S. international will miss up to 12 weeks with what manager Frank Lampard described as a "very serious quad injury."Americans in EnglandA World Cup on home soil now in the rearview mirror, a batch of U.S. men's national team players return to play with their clubs as the long road to the 2030 tournament officially gets underway. Wright will miss the beginning of the season but a handful of World Cup participants should be ready to go as soon as the opening whistle – starters like Crystal Palace's Chris Richards and Bournemouth's Tyler Adams are expected to play big roles this season again for their clubs, and the same goes for Fulham's Antonee Robinson and Leeds United's Brenden Aaronson. There's a new player to keep an eye on, too – 19-year-old winger Zavier Gozo joins Richards at Palace after beginning his career in MLS with Real Salt Lake, becoming the first of a new and exciting generation of U.S. players to take the next step up in his career.

title: The Nuggets are daring Nikola Jokić to leave after a listless summer - CBS Sports
description: Chances are Jokić -- a free agent next summer -- isn't going anywhere, but Denver isn't doing much to ensure that
body:
Chances are Jokić -- a free agent next summer -- isn't going anywhere, but Denver isn't doing much to ensure that
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Aug 21, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:08 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            9 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NBA's second apron claimed its latest casualty on Wednesday when the Denver Nuggets shipped Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers in an $88 million sign-and-trade that yielded the Nuggets nothing in the way of actual players. They got Cleveland's 2031 first-round pick and Sacramento's 2032 second-round pick, but no Watson replacement. On Friday, they pivoted to DeMar DeRozan. In 2026, Watson to DeRozan is a downgrade. If you believe otherwise, as the kids say, you don't know ball. Getting under the second apron is clearly the Nuggets' priority. They're not alone in this endeavor. The Knicks won last year's championship and immediately let Mitchell Robinson walk after owner James Dolan deemed any trip into the second apron as "suicidal." 
        
            
                Peyton Watson trade grades: Cavaliers grab breakout wing, Nuggets have serious questions around Nikola Jokić
                
                    Sam Quinn                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Robinson went to the Celtics, who have moved off of Jaylen Brown, Jrue Holiday, Kristaps Porziņģis, Al Horford and Luke Kornet since winning the 2024 title. Oklahoma City won the 2025 championship and just lost Aaron Wiggins, Lu Dort and Isaiah Joe this summer. The Warriors are currently driving their fans insane by playing it so tight to the vest since their 2022 title. The Bucks won in 2021 and have since blown up. All of this is to say, if the second apron has arguably made it easier than ever to put together a contending roster as talent has been spread more equitably across the league (I would argue no fewer than 13 teams will enter this coming season with conference-finals-caliber rosters). It has also made it harder than ever to keep these rosters together for the same reason.
Through this lens, the Nuggets having lost Bruce Brown, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Michael Porter Jr. and, now, Watson from that 2023 title team is no great sin. It pretty much happens to every team, barring some sort of one-off salary advantage like Jalen Brunson giving the Knicks a discount, or Stephen Curry signing a clearance-rack contract in 2012, or the Spurs having Victor Wembanyama (who has since also given San Antonio a long-term discount), Stephon Castle and Dylan Harper all on rookie contracts at the same time. The key, then, lies in the margin replacements. It's an extremely tight needle to thread, but fans look at a team like OKC -- which has nailed everything from adding Alex Caruso and Isaiah Hartenstein to drafting Cason Wallace and developing Ajay Mitchell, which has in turn afforded them the talent cushion to lose a starter in Dort and a two-way wing in Wiggins that every other team in the league would kill for without skipping a beat -- and expect their front offices to follow suit. This is where the Nuggets have fallen short. Again, they never found another 2023 Brown. They didn't want to pay Caldwell-Pope. They tried to swap Porter Jr. for Cam Johnson, thinking they fit the same player archetype, but it turned out Porter Jr. was just way better. Now they lose Watson, their one young, athletic player with the upside to represent at least a plausible path to improvement from last year's first-round-losing team, because they paid Christian Braun $125 million (at least double what he's worth) and couldn't stomach another money dump. 
Problem is, Watson "only" got $22 million annually, which isn't star money. That's regular starter money. Which Watson is, or should be, and being that the Nuggets were already over the second apron and thus crippled by the roster-building restrictions that apply anyway, why not just pay Watson? First of all, that's easy to say when it's not your money. Sure, the Kroenke family is reportedly worth almost $40 billion, but would running your 2026-27 payroll past $400 million -- which would be an NBA record and is what Denver would've been facing had it re-signed Watson at the $88 million he got from the Cavs -- have been a responsible decision for a team that would probably still fall short of true contender status? Probably not. Should they have done it anyway? The answer to that question would be a resounding no if the Nuggets didn't have Nikola Jokić still at the peak of his powers. But they do. And that's where this gets dicey. 
The franchise icon dilemmaWhen you have not just a superstar, but even one step up from that, a true franchise icon, it becomes impossible for fans to accept anything that could be even remotely perceived as organizational passivity, let alone an owner cheaping out. I'm not sure Denver has been passive, necessarily; I would, in fact, largely commend the Nuggets for their commitment to core continuity since the Aaron Gordon trade, which has indisputably served them well. It's also hard to say the owner of a repeater-tax team heading into next season with a nearly $300 million payroll has cheaped out. But yes, the Nuggets have cut some costly corners since the 2023 championship, and they're continuing to do so. No, fans are not going to accept that when their homegrown Hall of Famer is still arguably the greatest player in the world and currently set to become a free agent next summer. That's where having a player of this caliber can, in a weird way, go from a blessing to a curse as every season you're expected to set sail toward a championship even if the boat is starting to sink. It can become a suicide mission if you're not careful. Go ask the Bucks, who mortgaged everything but their soul to try to keep Giannis Antetokounmpo on a team whose window of contention had clearly closed. They waived and stretched Damian Lillard over five years, paying him $113 million to go play for the Blazers, all so they could turn around and pay Myles Turner north of $100 million. They had to trade Giannis anyway, and they'll be digging out from beneath that debt for years. 
That should've been an easy decision. The Bucks were done. The Nuggets are not, or don't have to be, but their margins have become impossibly thin as two younger, better teams in the Spurs and Thunder have risen to West prominence. Watson was a margin call. The guy has only started 64 games in his career. He had one big stretch last season during which his potential materialized, and his two-way upside is obvious, but it's also not unreasonable to not think he's worth an $88 million bet when you're already buried beneath the Braun contract as the only second-apron team in the league and probably not a contender anyway. Frankly, none of the margin calls the Nuggets have made over these last four summers have been unreasonable on their own. Brown was a big loss but the Nuggets couldn't have kept him if they wanted to in 2023 because they didn't have his early Bird rights and were limited in the raise they could offer him. When Indiana threw $45 million over two years at him, short of Brown taking about a $15 million haircut in the first year of his new deal, Denver, through no fault of its own, was out. The $66 million Orlando gave Caldwell-Pope proved pretty quickly to be a ridiculous contract. The Porter/Johnson swap looks bad in hindsight, but, at the time, pretty much everyone was in agreement that Porter was an overpaid third scorer and Johnson, who had just averaged 19 PPG on 39% 3-point shooting in Brooklyn, fit the bill of a similar player for almost half the price. The frustration, to whatever extent it exists, is in the aggregate of all these compromises. In addition to Watson, the Nuggets have also lost Jonas Valanciunas, who was at least somewhat of a plug for the non-Jokić minutes that have crippled Denver for years, and Sixth Man of the Year finalist Tim Hardaway Jr. from last year's team. 
Forgive the fans if the fans if they fail to see the excitement in adding Tyus Jones and Marvin Bagley Jr., and if they're starting, however quietly, to worriedly ponder a question that has always felt like a forgone conclusion. Will Jokić finish his career in Denver?All signs still point to yes. Two months ago, Jokić told Serbian reporters that his "desire is to play the rest of my life in Denver," and that he would "probably [re]sign [with the Nuggets] next year." That probably provides some pause, but Jokić opting not to sign the $278 million contract extension for which he was eligible this summer is very likely a purely financial decision. Next summer he can sign for $359 million. Chances are he will. He hasn't given any indication to the contrary. The concern would be if the Nuggets are taking this fact that Jokic has never threatened to leave for granted, using it as a license to downshift their roster aggression without fear of consequence. This is what has Golden State fans up in arms. No LeBron James team would hoard draft picks and focus on the "next era" because he would be threatening them behind closed doors within an inch of their organizational life. Stephen Curry doesn't do that. He stays in his lane and professes nothing but love and support for all the decisions his ownership and front office make, even if they come at the cost of his last shot at contention. 
Jokic has always appeared to be cut from the same go-along-get-along cloth. But to mistake that for a lack of competitive desire would be, well, a mistake. The idea that Jokic doesn't care about winning, or really even the sport of basketball in comparison to his horses, is rooted in romance rather than reality. It's fun to think about a Hall of Fame player not giving a damn, but it's not true. He wants to win. He wants to do it in Denver. But that's starting to look more and more unlikely as this core ages. You can only play the "if Aaron Gordon could just stay healthy" card for so long. What's funny is Curry's Warriors would be one of the teams that could theoretically pay Jokić next summer if they worked their cap sheet right. No doubt Joe Lacob is dreaming on that as we speak. It's about as likely to happen as the Warriors getting Giannis was. More likely is Jokić stays in Denver as they either fade more and more from contention or pull a rabbit out of the hat to get back into it -- perhaps by trading Jamal Murray or Gordon at the deadline, or even better, by attaching that 2031 Cleveland pick they got in the Watson deal to Braun and/or Johnson's expiring deal for a meaningful upgrade. 
Let's see how it goes. And again, chances are Jokić isn't going anywhere either way. But iI will say this: If ever there was a blueprint for forcing your franchise icon to consider relocation, it would look a lot like a summer in which you allow three significant players to go and replace them with Marvin freaking Bagley. It doesn't mean Jokić is going to leave. I can't state that enough. But until further notice, it sort of feels like the Nuggets are daring him to do so.

title: Serie A Power Rankings: Inter start on top, AC Milan back on track; Fiorentina set to surprise - CBS Sports
description: Serie A is finally back! The 2026-2027 Serie A season will kick off this weekend in Italy, with Inter, the 2025-2026 Scudetto winners, l
body:
Serie A is finally back! The 2026-2027 Serie A season will kick off this weekend in Italy, with Inter, the 2025-2026 Scudetto winners, looking to defend the title in the new season. AC Milan, their cross-city rivals, made some key signings in the summer after replacing the coach and the whole club hierarchy after the disappointing end of the last campaign, and appointed former Manchester United coach Ruben Amorim to lead the new cycle. Six teams replaced their coaches, including Napoli, which saw Antonio Conte leave the Azzurri after two seasons and appointed former AC Milan and Juventus manager Massimiliano Allegri. Let's take a look at our power rankings ahead of the upcoming season: 1. Inter The 2025-2026 Serie A champions are still the favorites to replicate the success of the past season. They lost a key player in Denzel Dumfries, who joined Real Madrid, but replaced him with Djed Spence and signed other players like John Stones and Curtis Jones who can help Cristian Chivu win another Scudetto. Overall, they have a stronger squad compared to the one that won the most recent Serie A title. 2. AC Milan The Rossoneri spent big money in the summer to support American Christian Pulisic and signed striker Goncalo Ramos from PSG who became the highest paid player in the history of the club, after Gerry Cardinale's side spent over $70 million to sign the Portuguese striker. On top of him, they also signed Mario Gila from Lazio for around $20 million and Diego Moreira from Strasbourg for more than $60 million. However, the biggest decision was to appoint Ruben Amorim to replace Massimiliano Allegri, who failed to bring the Rossoneri back to Champions League soccer. 3. NapoliIt didn't take long time for Allegri to find a new club as Napoli decided to hire him after Antonio Conte's decision to leave the Azzurri ahead of the summer. Allegri, who has signed a three-year deal with the Italian club, will be expected to improve Napoli's performances, particularly in the Champions League, as demanded by club owner Aurelio De Laurentiis. Napoli have a strong squad, but last season their campaign was severely affected by injuries.
4. AS Roma  The side coached by Gian Piero Gasperini clinched a Champions League spot at the end of a successful campaign, but it will now be much more complicated to replicate the same success. They have a chance to make a deep run, and the roster is also strong enough to achieve the targets requested by the fan base and the ownership. Winning a trophy, maybe the Coppa Italia, could be a major milestone for the new project, now entering its second year, led by the former Atalanta manager. 5. Como Como were one of the biggest surprises of the 2025–26 season but maybe not entirely unexpectedly. Their fourth-place finish and historic qualification for the Champions League were remarkable, but the team led by Cesc Fabregas wants more. They re-signed Nico Paz from Real Madrid for $60 million, arguably the most important Serie A signing of the summer. The only doubt about them is how they will deal with the two major competitions at the same time, but watch out for them, once again. 6. JuventusDespite confirming head coach Luciano Spalletti for at least another season, everything has changed again at the club with a new CEO in Giovanni Carnevali, an experienced Italian director who can lead the new cycle. Some of the signings were interesting, such as the one of Kerim Alajbegovic from Bayer Leverkusen or the one of Randal Kolo Muani from PSG. Others, like the one of Guglielmo Vicario on loan from Tottenham as the new starting goalkeeper, are not what we expected. 
7. FiorentinaI strongly believe they will be the surprise of the season, after risking relegation last year. Former Tottenham and Juventus director Fabio Paratici is leading the sporting project and has signed multiple talents, starting with Franco Mastantuono on loan from Real Madrid, and appointed a young talented coach like Fabio Grosso, who previously coached Sassuolo in the Italian first division. Fiorentina might finally be back. 8. AtalantaNothing against the club and the job they've done over the past years, but when you sign a coach like Maurizio Sarri you can expect your team to perform more on the long term, missing out some key points in the first part of the season. This is why I think they can aim for European soccer, but it won't be that easy. 9. GenoaAnother team I think will do well. Under Daniele De Rossi's management, Genoa were a surprising side in the second part of the season, and in his full campaign in charge I think there's a big chance to see them as one of the surprises of the Serie A season. 
10. BolognaIt will be difficult for them after Vincenzo Italiano decided to leave the Italian side to join Besiktas. They hired a coach like Domenico Tedesco, who will make his Serie A debut this weekend: A risky choice. 11. UdineseOne of those teams that always seem to find themselves in the same position at the start of the season: unlikely to face a relegation battle, but equally unlikely to challenge for a European spot.12. Torino I'm curious to see the impact of Ignazio Abate in Serie A after bringing Juve Stabia, a team that was placed under judicial administration as prosecutors stated the Serie B club was used as a tool by the local Camorra mafia clan, to the playoffs last season; now he has his first big chance in the Italian top flight. 
13. SassuoloGiovanni Carnevali, the former club CEO and the mastermind behind the success of the Neroverdi in the past years, has left his position and joined Juventus this summer. While Fabio Grosso left the club to take over at Fiorentina and most of the key players stayed, the club appointed Alberto Aquilani as his successor. Aquilani, who led Catanzaro to the Serie B playoff final in June, is widely regarded as one of the most talented young managers in Italy.14. ParmaThe Crociati survived the Italian first division under Carlos Cuesta last season, the youngest coach in the league and aim to do the same this year despite selling some key players, such as Zion Suzuki and Gabriel Strefezza. 15. CagliariThe first season under Vincenzo Pisacane was a success overall as the team managed to avoid relegation, and this season we can expect more from them, but it won't be easier. 
16. LazioThere are not many hopes around Lazio this season after hiring Gennaro Gattuso as the new head coach. The Biancocelesti had another disappointing summer transfer window, as they saw some key players leaving such as Mario Gila who joined AC Milan and had to face a net-zero transfer window for the summer 2026 session. In this worrying financial environment, a tumble down the table is a real possibility17. VeneziaTheir plans for a new stadium are already underway, but if you get the chance to go and watch a match at the current Penzo Stadium, do it. It's an unforgettable experience.18. MonzaThe club made some signings in the summer, but none of them are capable of keeping the team in the first division. Am I too drastic? Probably not. 
19. LecceEusebio Di Francesco finally managed to keep Lecce in the top flight after suffering relegation twice in two years with Frosinone and Venezia. However, I think keeping them up this time will be an even bigger challenge.20. FrosinoneThis is what Massimiliano Alvini, the head coach, said about the transfer window. "I wasn't involved. As the coach, you have to understand the characteristics of the new signings. It will take time, months, to fully integrate them." I don't see them avoiding relegation, do you?

        After receiving a fifth year of eligibility, former Florida State quarterback Thomas Castellanos has entered the NCAA transfer portal, sources tell CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz.On Friday, a Kentucky judge granted a temporary injunction in an eligibility lawsuit that included Castellanos and former Missouri basketball standout Mark Mitchell. Because Castellanos now has an injunction, he will not be affected by the new ruling in the Colorado lawsuit that took away eligibility for qualified athletes in the class of 2022.A three-star recruit out of Georgia, Castellanos signed with UCF as a member of the 2022 recruiting class. The following season, Castellanos transferred to Boston College, where he started across two seasons before jumping to Florida State as a senior in 2025.Last year, Castellanos completed 58.3% of his passes for 2,760 yards, 15 touchdowns and nine interceptions while also rushing for 557 yards and nine touchdowns. While Castellanos' lone season with the Seminoles was turbulent, he led the team to an upset of No. 8 Alabama in Week 1.Throughout his college career, Castellanos has provided dynamic playmaking with his legs, and he even rushed for 1,113 yards as a sophomore at Boston College. Despite missing spring practice and most of fall camp, Castellanos has already reportedly generated significant interest from at least one Power Four team.
Where will Castellanos land?Texas Tech has emerged as the most likely landing spot for Castellanos as he looks to continue his college career, according to multiple reports. Given how the quarterback situation has evolved in Lubbock throughout the offseason, landing with the Red Raiders makes plenty of sense for Castellanos.Texas Tech paid up to land Cincinnati transfer Brendan Sorsby out of the transfer portal, but due to fallout from a gambling scandal, Sorsby will no longer play for the Red Raiders this fall. Will Hammond — very talented in his own right — is now the starter, but he's coming off a torn ACL he suffered last October.While the Red Raiders are still fine at the top of the quarterback depth chart, the loss of Sorsby made them much shallower. Sophomore Lloyd Jones III is currently set to back up Hammond, but he's attempted just five passes at the college level. Castellanos would give Texas Tech more insurance at the most important position on the field.
That's important because the rest of the Texas Tech roster looks to be a legitimate College Football Playoff threat. The Red Raiders brought in 22 players via the portal, and that class ranked No. 6 nationally, according to 247Sports. Castellanos would help ensure that those title hopes won't be immediately derailed if Hammond is unable to play.
